assumptions: the strategy game is optimal (Cusenza et al. 2022, Thm 1.2) - needed only to call its length L(n); the identity with the simulated strategy game is unconditional
random samples with a fixed seed
meta.falsification: Any mismatch with full simulation (would contradict Theorems 1-2), any violated bound, or any n where the recursion and the method disagree (would refute CLM-C19-05).
meta.hypothesis: Theorem 7 of proofs/paper/C19.md: the method equals the strategy game length for every n, with at most 1 + (t + 1)(t + 6)/2 second-phase moves; CLM-C19-05 (conjecture) agrees with it everywhere.
meta.methodology: Compare with greedy_length_fast for every n < 20000; compare longest_rec (the recursion) with the method for every n < 100000, 3000 random n in [1e6, 1e15) and 800 n = F_j + m (j = 30..69, m < F_(j-1)); check second-phase moves <= B(n) - Psi(lazy(n)) <= 1 + (t + 1)(t + 6)/2 on all tested n; time the method, the recursion and (n <= 1e7) full simulation.
meta.question: Does L(n) = Psi(lazy(n)) + (second phase from lazy(n)) agree with full simulation, does the move bound hold, and does the conjectured recursion agree with this provably correct method on far more n than before?
meta.title: The lazy-representation method for the longest Zeckendorf game: correctness checks, the move bound, and the recursion CLM-C19-05 tested against it

summary: method vs full simulation, every n < 20000: 0 mismatches
recursion CLM-C19-05 vs the method on 103799 n (all n < 1e5, 3000 random n < 1e15, 800 F_j + m): 0 mismatches
second-phase moves <= B(n) - Psi(lazy(n)) <= 1 + (t+1)(t+6)/2 on every tested n: violations 0; largest B - Psi(lazy) relative to the bound 0.476 (n = 89287158190794)
